surprises.description: The preview put Q3 core EPS at $0.48, with $0.45–$0.46 in its bear case. ARCC reported $0.46, two cents below consensus and at the low end of that bear-case range.

ARCC announced an acquisition the preview did not anticipate: MFIC will add over 200 portfolio companies and is expected to be modestly accretive to core EPS. The purchase uses a deeper discount to NAV, with the discount concentrated in a small portion of higher-uncertainty investments.
surprises.fact_evidence: “ARCC announced an agreement to acquire” MFIC, “expected to be modestly accretive to core EPS,” adding “over 200 portfolio companies”; it is “being purchased at a deeper discount to NAV,” with the discount “concentrated in a small percentage of higher-uncertainty investments.”

surprises.description: Q3 originations slowed to $2.1 billion and the closing ratio was moderately below its historical average, a weaker conversion outcome than the preview’s pipeline-focused setup suggested. Management attributed this to greater selectivity and a slower deal environment.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 originations slowed to $2.1 billion with a closing ratio moderately below the historical ~5% average,” attributed to “increased selectivity and a slower overall deal environment.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview noted “Q2 deal reviews +25% sequentially; June was ‘one of our strongest months in two years.’ Did that convert?” and identified whether the “June pipeline converts” as a key scenario driver.

surprises.description: Despite the slower Q3, post-quarter activity was notably strong: $1.1 billion of Q4 commitments had already closed and the backlog was about $2.5 billion, described as historically strong. This offers a more constructive near-term pipeline signal than the Q3 slowdown alone would suggest.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Post-quarter momentum is strong, with $1.1 billion of commitments already closed in Q4 and an investment backlog of approximately $2.5 billion, described as historically strong levels.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview asked whether the pipeline would convert and listed “net portfolio growth” as a bull-case driver, but did not forecast this level of Q4 commitments or backlog.

surprises.description: New first-lien spreads widened 50 basis points quarter over quarter, a stronger improvement in lending terms than the preview’s cited 20-basis-point increase in new senior loan spreads since Q4’25. Leverage on new loans also decreased by 0.5 turn.
surprises.fact_evidence: “First lien spreads on new originations widened 50 basis points quarter-over-quarter while leverage levels decreased by 0.5 turn, reflecting improved lending market conditions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview cited “new senior loan spreads +20bp vs. Q4’25” and highlighted spread and funding-cost trends as key items to watch.

surprises.description: Net leverage came in below the preview’s 1.12x figure, at 1.06x (1.10x pro forma for an unsettled trade), while available liquidity was about $7 billion versus the preview’s roughly $6.0 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net leverage was 1.06x (1.10x pro forma for an unsettled trade), with ~$7 billion of available liquidity.”
